notable_absence.finding: The SYNOPSIS line names the WRONG subcommand outright: '_couchbase-cli setting-enable_ [--cluster <url>] ...' - every other page in this batch, and this page's own title, description, OPTIONS and EXAMPLES, consistently say `setting-encryption`, but the SYNOPSIS's italicized command name is the literal string `setting-enable`. This is the single most direct piece of authorship-provenance evidence found in this batch: a copy-paste artifact (most likely from an earlier or sibling subcommand's SYNOPSIS template) that a TW review pass would very likely have caught, left uncorrected in a published reference page. Separately, OPTIONS defines the rotate flag as '\--rotate <keyid>\n\nRotate the given key.' at the very end of the OPTIONS list, but the SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION's mutually-exclusive-argument list, and every EXAMPLES invocation ('--rotate-key 2') all use the longer name `--rotate-key` - so the OPTIONS entry for this flag is itself inconsistently named relative to the rest of its own page, a second, smaller instance of the same drift.

cross_component_finding: The 'setting-enable' SYNOPSIS typo, taken together with setting-compaction's '--meta-data-purge-interval' EXAMPLES typo and setting-notification's --enable-notification/--enable-notifications singular/plural mismatch, means 3 of the 8 pages read in this batch carry a literal command-name-or-flag-name inconsistency between their own SYNOPSIS/OPTIONS and their own EXAMPLES/DESCRIPTION - never a factual error about behavior, always a spelling/naming slip, which is precisely the terse-prose-and-light-review signature this round's framing predicted for cli/ as opposed to the rest of the Server docs tree.
cross_product_finding: Encryption-at-rest key management here (add-key/edit-key/rotate-key/delete-key, KEK vs DEK, KMIP and AWS KMS integration, auto-rotation with an ISO 8601 start date) is described as a purely Server/on-prem CLI-and-cluster-local feature with no reference to Capella's own at-rest encryption model or to whether Capella exposes an equivalent key-management surface at all - consistent with encryption:native-encryption-at-rest's registry note that it is an Enterprise Edition Server feature, but this page gives no signal either way about Capella parity, so no cross-product claim beyond 'silent on Capella' can be made.
